description: Visual (vision-language) CANDIDATES for offline evaluation only (PR-AI-VL-220, decision D22). This file is deliberately separate from config/ai_model_registry.json: that registry feeds the in-app model selector, Preview enablement and import-model, all of which treat an entry as a text model, so a visual entry there would be offered for text use. Nothing in src/ or in the production import-model, activation, selector or Preview path reads this file; a test proves it. Every candidate is unqualified, not production eligible, not text-registry eligible and has NO approved image invocation (the proposed invocation is a separate document that needs explicit owner approval). Sizes and SHA-256 are the Hugging Face LFS values reviewed on 2026-11-14 and verified against the locally downloaded bytes the same day. Every source is pinned to a 40-character commit revision, never a branch. Nothing is downloaded by the application.

candidates.display_name: LFM3-VL-2B Q4_K_M with F16 vision projector (Liquid AI GGUF)
candidates.converter: Liquid AI GGUF export (converter build is not stated in the repository metadata)

projector.selection_basis: The publisher states that every mmproj file in the repository is used unchanged across language-model quantizations (the model card's NVFP4 section) and benchmarks edge inference with a Q4_0 language model and an F16 projector. F16 is pinned so the vision front end is not a second quantization variable in the comparison. The projector's declared base model equals the language model's, and its projection_dim (2048) equals the language model's embedding_length (2048).

runtime.basis: The publisher's model card requires llama.cpp b11960 or newer. The llama.cpp source at tag b11840 has no lfm3vl projector (tools/mtmd/clip-impl.h) and tag b11960 does (reviewed as text; no binary was run). llama-mtmd-cli.exe is already hashed in the pinned b11960-cpu file map.

known_limits: Vendor benchmarks do not establish StableNew quality; nothing here claims superiority over the Qwen3.5 or LFM3 text models.
The LFM Open License v1.0 caps commercial use by an entity at a revenue threshold; the owner must acknowledge this exact license text before any import.
No inference has been run; image invocation is not approved.
